source_name: Addiko Bank AD Podgorica – corporate website (bank NOT in the original cell list)
why_relevant: Snowballed find: EBRD reporting confirms Addiko Bank Podgorica is an active Montenegrin bank and an EBRD client under the 'Go Digital in the Western Balkans' programme (loan up to EUR 2m for SME support). It was missing from the cell's bank list and is a live digital-transformation buyer, so it must be added to the ME bank actor map.

source_name: CBCG – Registar banaka / Banke u Crnoj Gori (Central Bank of Montenegro register of banks)
why_relevant: The authoritative, regulator-maintained list of every licensed bank in Montenegro with its official name and website link. This is the master key that resolves the exact domains for the whole private-buyer universe (including banks missing from the cell brief, e.g. Addiko) and keeps the actor map current as banks merge or rebrand. Highest-value pointer for this cell.

source_name: Bankar.me – Montenegrin banking and finance news portal
why_relevant: Specialist Montenegrin banking trade press. It reports bank product launches, technology projects, association events (e.g. it covered the UBCG gathering of all 11 member banks) and vendor partnerships — the practical substitute for the procurement notices Montenegrin private banks never publish. Local-language, high frequency, and it names both banks and their technology partners.

source_name: Montenegroberza (Montenegro Stock Exchange) – issuer disclosures for listed banks
why_relevant: Several Montenegrin banks are listed issuers and must file material-event disclosures, annual reports and public calls (javni poziv) through the exchange. This turns part of an otherwise-private bank's activity — capital raises tied to IT investment programmes, major contracts, related-party supplier transactions — into a structured, dated, machine-readable filing stream. Complements the CBCG register.

source_name: Informacije Crna Gora – 'Javni poziv' aggregation page
why_relevant: A Montenegrin aggregator that collects items tagged 'javni poziv'. It surfaced as a top hit on two separate local-language procurement queries, which suggests it indexes public calls beyond the state portal — including calls published by banks and other non-public-sector bodies (e.g. the Razvojna banka real-estate call). Useful as a low-cost catch-all for the phrase that private ME banks actually use.

source_name: Razvojna banka Crne Gore / IRF – public calls (state-owned development bank, contrast case)
why_relevant: Confirmed via search: Razvojna banka Crne Gore AD publishes sealed-bid public calls ('Ponuda ne otvaraj') with named submission addresses and opening dates. Because it is state-owned it DOES fall under public procurement rules, unlike the commercial banks in this cell. It is therefore both a genuine tender source in its own right and the benchmark that shows what the private banks are deliberately not publishing. Note IRF/Razvojna banka shares are being listed on the regulated market per Montenegrin press, which adds a disclosure stream.

source_name: eKapija – regional (RS/ME) business portal, banking-IT contract coverage
why_relevant: Confirmed to publish vendor-side contract news for regional banking IT (e.g. an Asseco SEE core-banking contract story). Montenegrin banks belong to regional groups (NLB, OTP, Erste, Addiko) whose vendor contracts are usually announced regionally, in Serbian, on portals like this rather than on the ME bank's own site. This is a realistic substitute for missing ME award notices.

source_name: Montenegrin general press economy desks – Vijesti, Pobjeda, Dan, RTCG
why_relevant: Montenegro's mainstream outlets carry the bank-sector stories that never appear on bank websites: ATM network changes, branch/technology investments, ownership changes, disputes over contracts. RTCG (public broadcaster) and Dan were both confirmed to publish economy coverage naming banks and financial institutions. Low precision, high recall — the backstop layer for a cell with no primary procurement feed.

source_name: EU Delegation to Montenegro – contract award notices (EEAS)
why_relevant: The EU Delegation publishes Montenegrin-language 'Obavještenje o dodjeli ugovora o uslugama' (service contract award notices). Where EU-funded technical assistance touches the banking/payments sector (SME finance, digitalisation, payment-system alignment with the EU acquis), these award notices name the winning contractors and give the only public award record involving ME financial-sector work. Confirmed to exist in Montenegrin.

source_name: OTP Bank Nyrt. — Szállítóknak (Supplier page, SAP Ariba onboarding)
why_relevant: Group-parent supplier gateway of OTP Group, owner of CKB Banka (Crnogorska komercijalna banka AD Podgorica), the largest bank in Montenegro. Page states OTP Bank is progressively rolling out SAP Ariba for procurement processes and hosts supplier onboarding requirements, DORA ICT-security training obligations for vendors and a Partner Ethics Code. This is where a vendor wanting to sell payments/IT into the Montenegrin subsidiary must first be registered at group level.

source_name: SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network — OTP Bank buyer instance (supplier registration)
why_relevant: OTP Bank's own supplier page names SAP Ariba as the procurement system being rolled out. Sourcing events for OTP Group entities (which would include CKB Montenegro spend where group-sourced) are issued through this platform. Registration on the buyer's Ariba instance is the practical channel through which a Montenegrin-relevant group RFP would be received.

source_name: SAP Business Network Discovery (public buyer postings)
why_relevant: Where an Ariba-using buyer such as OTP posts an open (non-invitation) buying need, the posting surfaces on Business Network Discovery and is visible to registered suppliers. A cheap early-warning channel for group-level IT/payments demand that may cascade to the Montenegrin subsidiary.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H.) — group procurement subsidiary page
why_relevant: EGP explicitly manages the entire external spend of all majority-owned entities within Erste Group, which includes Erste Bank AD Podgorica (Montenegro). The page hosts supplier-facing documents: general supplier terms, NDA template, audit questionnaire, performance and sustainability scorecards, whistleblower procedure — i.e. the actual rulebook a vendor must satisfy to be contracted for Montenegro. HQ Vienna, Am Belvedere 1; subsidiaries in CZ, HU, SK, RO, HR.

source_name: erstegroupprocurement.com (EGP vanity domain, 301 to erstegroup.com)
why_relevant: Canonical vanity domain cited in third-party profiles as the EGP website. Observed to 301-redirect to the erstegroup.com procurement page, so it is a stable alias worth pinning in a monitor list; if EGP ever stands up a standalone supplier portal it will most likely reappear here.

source_name: Erste Group — Press releases / News & Media
why_relevant: Group-level technology, payments and platform decisions (and M&A that resets vendor landscapes, e.g. the May 2025 Santander Bank Polska stake announcement) are announced here long before any Montenegrin-level visibility. Buying signal for a group-rolled-out platform typically appears as a strategy/partnership press release, not a tender notice.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica — corporate site (Montenegrin subsidiary of Erste Group)
why_relevant: Subsidiary endpoint of group-sourced contracts. No procurement/tender section was found, which is itself the confirming evidence for this cell's hypothesis: buying decisions sit in Vienna. Still worth tracking for new-product launches (cards, POS, mobile wallet) that reveal which group-selected vendor landed in Montenegro. Note the site is served from cdn0.erstegroup.com, i.e. group-managed infrastructure.

source_name: NLB Group — Javni razpisi (public calls)
why_relevant: The only public 'razpisi' channel of NLB d.d., parent of NLB Banka AD Podgorica. Inspected content: the published calls are for the sale of receivables/claims against debtors (e.g. Slimeks d.o.o. v stečaju), not goods/services/IT procurement. Track it anyway because it is the single named NLB tender channel and category drift is possible; and NPL sale calls are themselves a distinct A2 signal.

source_name: NLB Group — Press releases / Media Center
why_relevant: NLB does not publish operational IT tenders, so group technology and platform decisions covering the Montenegrin subsidiary surface as press releases. Also the authoritative source for group market structure (six subsidiary banks; NLB holds ~99.87% of NLB Banka AD Podgorica), which anchors the actor map.

source_name: OTP Group — Investor Relations & News (otpgroup.info)
why_relevant: OTP Group's dedicated IR/news domain, separate from the Hungarian retail site. Group-level technology programmes, subsidiary integrations and extraordinary announcements land here first; CKB Montenegro is reported inside group segment disclosure rather than locally. Also the correct entry point after the otpbank.hu/portal/en/IRandPR path proved to resolve to the retail portal rather than a press archive.

source_name: CKB Banka (Crnogorska komercijalna banka AD Podgorica, member of OTP Group) — corporate site
why_relevant: Largest bank in Montenegro by loans, deposits and clients; OTP-owned since 2006; 26 branches, 115 ATMs. Its own site carries no tender section, confirming procurement sits with OTP group functions. The ATM/card estate size makes it the single most material demand point in Montenegro for self-service and card-processing vendors, so its product announcements are the visible tail of a Budapest-level decision.

source_name: OTP banka d.d. (Croatia) — group expansion news on Montenegro
why_relevant: Illustrates the pattern this cell exists to capture: a Montenegro-relevant corporate/structural announcement published by a sister/parent entity in another country, in Croatian, not by the Montenegrin bank. Sister-bank newsrooms (HR, RS, SI) are an under-watched channel for ME-affecting group decisions.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG — Corporate Governance Reports (Group Procurement Policy disclosure)
why_relevant: Addiko Group (Vienna, Canettistraße 5) runs banks in HR, SI, RS, BA and Montenegro. Addiko publishes no supplier portal, but its Corporate Governance and Annual Reports disclose that a Group procurement policy applies to all Addiko Group entities and covers procurement orders above a defined threshold — i.e. documentary proof that Montenegrin above-threshold IT/payments buying is decided in Vienna, plus the threshold structure itself.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG — Investor Relations & Group Annual Reports
why_relevant: Group Annual Reports (2022–2025 consolidated financial reports available as PDFs) carry IT/administrative expense breakdowns, outsourcing and supplier/sustainability sections, and segment reporting that isolates Montenegro. Best available quantitative proxy for group-level IT spend that will be routed to the Montenegrin subsidiary, given Addiko publishes no tenders at all.
